answer: Juror-vouched registration bond: a new account burns 3 POA and locks 20 POA for 50 epochs, released only if 3 randomly drawn established accounts each stake 1 POA to vouch after a live cipher challenge. An honest user pays 3 burned and 20 locked; 1,000 fakes burn 3,000 and lock 20,000 POA while needing 3,000 vouches. Attackers could vouch for each other, but random draws from thousands of established accounts rarely pick them, and a vouch for a failed challenge forfeits the 1 POA stake. A public atlas of vouches lets auditors flag clusters, and a gale of registrations raises the burn.
